title: Statin mechanism at pharmacology-lecture level

turns.content: I'm a pharmacist with a PhD. Don't explain what cholesterol is. Give me the mechanism of action of statins at the level of a pharmacology lecture: target, what happens to hepatic regulation, and the effect on LDL receptors. Compact please.

rationale: Opposite of the child-level test: the audience is an expert, so the right answer is technical and compact (1.6, 1.3). Over-simplifying or adding beginner explanations fails.

provenance.summary: Models tend to use a uniform explanatory register regardless of audience. Statins' mechanism is well established, and the details are in standard pharmacology references.

sources.title: Statin (mechanism of action)
sources.supports: Statins competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase; reduced hepatic cholesterol leads to more LDL receptors.
sources.quote: act by competitively inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of the mevalonate pathway

expected_behavior: Uses precise terminology and skips basics: competitive inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, reduced hepatic cholesterol synthesis, compensatory SREBP-2-mediated upregulation of LDL receptors and increased LDL clearance (1.6, 1.2). Compact, no beginner definitions (1.3).
reference_answer:
Statins are competitive inhibitors of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of the mevalonate pathway; they are structural analogues of HMG-CoA and occupy its active site.

Hepatic effect: reduced mevalonate flux lowers intracellular sterol pools. The fall in hepatic cholesterol activates SREBP-2 (released after SCAP-dependent transport and proteolytic cleavage), which upregulates transcription of the LDL receptor gene and HMG-CoA reductase itself.

Plasma effect: more hepatic LDL receptors increase clearance of LDL and, via apoE binding, VLDL remnants (IDL), which lowers plasma LDL-C. Reduced hepatic VLDL output contributes. Because synthesis peaks at night, short-half-life statins (simvastatin) are often dosed in the evening.

Pleiotropic effects through reduced isoprenoid intermediates (e.g. Rho/Ras prenylation) are discussed but their clinical weight is debated.
must_include: hepatic cholesterol decrease leads to LDL receptor upregulation (SREBP-2)

rubric.criterion: Covers target, hepatic regulation, LDL receptor

key_facts.claim: Statins act by competitively inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase.

review.notes: Wikipedia statin article confirms competitive inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase and SREBP/LDL receptor mechanism.
